newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania oil output slightly down in September.
newsitem.headline: Romania oil output slightly down in September.

text.p: Romanian crude oil production dropped to 551,893 tonnes in September from 573,462 tonnes in August and was 1.0 percent down from September 1995, the Industry Ministry said on Monday.
The Ministry's oil and gas department said gas output in September was 1.32 billion cubic metres, some 5.0 million up from August but around 9.0 percent down from the previous year.

Romania plans to maintain crude extraction this year close to the 1995 level of 6.7 million tonnes but it will have to resort to large imports to meet domestic demand and keep its 12 refineries operating at a minimum.
Ministry data show Romania processed 8.7 million tonnes of crude over January-August, when imports amounted to 4.69 million tonnes.

Oil refining this year involves a total 14.5 million tonnes, against 15.2 million tonnes processed in its underused refineries last year. Romania's refineries have a total capacity of 34 million tonnes.
Bucharest recently guaranteed a $200 million loan arranged with Chase Manhattan for crude imports by the state Romanian Oil Company over the next few months.

In a bid to revive crude production -- which has declined over the past 20 years from 14 million tonnes peaks in the early 1970s -- Romania has launched a licensing round for 15 onshore and offshore prospective oil blocks.

Some 50 oil operators have already submitted bids, while others are expected to do so before an end-October deadline. Successful bidders will be announced next January, with work on the blocks scheduled to start next June.
